To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
salts of organic acids can protect frost sensitive thylakoids against freezing damage.
salts of organic acids can protect thylakoid (chloroplast) membranes during freezing.
salts of organic acids can protect thylakoid membrane integrity during freezing, but that this effect is unspecific and depends on the presence of other salts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of organic acids on membrane stability during freezing.
the effect of organic acids on thylakoids during freezing.
the effect of salts of various organic and inorganic acids on thylakoids in the course of and after freezing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
organic acids are effective in protecting thylakoid structure during freezing, but that the protective mechanism remains to be elucidated.
organic acids can protect membranes during freezing and thawing, but the mechanism of the protective effect remains to be elucidated.
the protective effect of salts of certain organic acids during freezing of thylakoids is a combination of colligative and specific effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
organic acids can protect thylakoid systems against membrane inactivation by electrolytes, both during freezing and at temperatures above the freezing range.
the presence of salts, especially of organic acids, can prevent the membrane inactivation during freezing, but the effect is dependent on the ratio of inorganic to organic salt.
organic acids can protect chloroplasts against freezing injury only if the membranes have previously been damaged by high salt concentrations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the addition of salts of organic or inorganic acids to the freezing medium can prevent the inactivation of chloroplast thylakoid membrane during freezing and thawing.
organic acids, especially in the presence of high electrolyte concentrations, are able to protect thylakoid membrane integrity against freezing.
the presence of salts in the medium can be used to protect chloroplasts from freezing injury.
